questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Hydrologic Cycle & Catchment Characteristics
questions.text: Explain the Hydrologic Cycle with a neat block diagram and water budget equation: $P - R - G - E - T = \Delta S$. Explain methods for estimating missing precipitation data: (a) Arithmetic Mean Method, and (b) Normal Ratio Method ($P_x = \frac{N_x}{m}\sum \frac{P_i}{N_i}$).

Explain methods to calculate Mean Areal Rainfall over a catchment: (a) Arithmetic Average Method, (b) Thiessen Polygon Method, and (c) Isohyetal Method. Explain Double Mass Curve analysis for checking consistency of rainfall records.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Hydrologic Cycle & Catchment Characteristics
questions.text: Explain Horton's Infiltration Equation: $f_p = f_c + (f_0 - f_c)e^{-k t}$. Define $\phi$-Index and $W$-Index. A 6-hour storm produces rainfall increments of $1.5, 2.5, 4.0, 3.0, 1.8, 1.2\,\text{cm/hr}$. If total runoff depth is $6.5\,\text{cm}$, determine the $\phi$-index of the catchment.
Explain Streamflow Measurement methods: Area-Velocity Method using Current Meter (0.2D & 0.8D point methods), Dilution Gauging (Tracer method), and Stage-Discharge Rating Curve ($Q = C_r(G - a)^b$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Hydrograph Analysis & Unit Hydrograph Theory
questions.text: Define Unit Hydrograph (UH). State the underlying assumptions of Unit Hydrograph Theory (Linear response and Time invariance). Describe base flow separation methods (Straight line method, Fixed base method, Variable slope method).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Hydrograph Analysis & Unit Hydrograph Theory
questions.text: Given the ordinates of a 4-hour Unit Hydrograph at 2-hour intervals: $[0, 12, 35, 60, 48, 30, 18, 8, 0]\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, derive the ordinates of a 6-hour Unit Hydrograph for the same catchment using the S-Curve (Summation Hydrograph) method.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Flood Routing & Flood Frequency Analysis
questions.text: Explain the Muskingum Channel Flood Routing Method ($Q_{j+1} = C_0 I_{j+1} + C_1 I_j + C_2 Q_j$ where $C_0 + C_1 + C_2 = 1$). Route a given inflow flood hydrograph through a river reach with parameters $K = 12\,\text{hours}$ and $x = 0.2$ with routing time step $\Delta t = 6\,\text{hours}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Flood Routing & Flood Frequency Analysis
questions.text: Explain Gumbel's Extreme Value Distribution Method for flood frequency analysis: $x_T = \bar{x} + K_T \sigma_x$ where $K_T = \frac{y_T - \bar{y}_n}{S_n}$ and $y_T = -\ln\left[-\ln\left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)\right]$. Calculate the 50-year and 100-year return period peak floods for a river with 30 years of annual maximum flood data (Mean $\bar{x} = 1200\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$, Standard deviation $\sigma_x = 350\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$).

Derive Dupuit-Thiem Equations for steady-state radial flow to a fully penetrating well in: (a) Unconfined Aquifer ($Q = \frac{\pi K (h_2^2 - h_1^2)}{\ln(r_2/r_1)}$), and (b) Confined Aquifer ($Q = \frac{2\pi K b (h_2 - h_1)}{\ln(r_2/r_1)}$). What is Specific Yield ($S_y$) and Specific Retention ($S_r$)?
